exposure: Visually impaired women due to possible autoimmune etiology
visual impairment due to autoimmune etiology
outcome: Maternal complications (gestational diabetes, severe preeclampsia, preterm delivery, cesarean section, packed cell transfusion)
cohort: 265,741 deliveries, including 80 in visually impaired women, at a single center between 1988-2012
finding: Visually impaired pregnant women had higher rates of cesarean section and packed cell transfusion, but perinatal outcomes were comparable to the general population.
mod_finding: Visually impaired women had a significantly higher rate of cesarean section compared to women without visual impairment (OR 2.04, 95% CI 1.23-3.37, p=0.006).
